A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relativistic separable potentials elaborating the complex separable kernel, make it possible for the first time to describe simultaneously the elastic and inelastic parts (phase shifts, the low-energy parameters, the inelasticity parameters) of the neutron– proton interaction in the whole energy range from threshold to 3 GeV, and the dibaryon resonant structures in the P 3 partial-wave states.
a good description of the elastic and inelastic neutron–proton data is obtained with the use of our separable potentials in the energy range from the threshold to 3 GeV.
the relativistic complex separables are able to describe all the main features of the neutron– proton interaction in the energy range up to 3 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complex separable kernel is a good tool for the analysis of the experimental data for both the elastic and inelastic parts of the neutron– proton scattering.
the relativistic multirank separability approach is a very powerful method to describe the nucleon–nucleon interaction.
the inelasticity of the NN interaction can be described by a separable complex kernel with a single rank.
